title: Executive functions as a transdiagnostic endophenotype in developmental psychopathology
title_zh: 执行功能作为发展性精神病理学的跨诊断内在表型
abstract: Abstract The majority of mental health conditions emerges before adulthood, with prevalence increasing especially during childhood and adolescence. Coupled with high comorbidity between disorders, there is an urgent need to identify transdiagnostic mechanisms that underpin both risk and resilience to developmental psychopathology. Here we propose executive functions (EFs), a set of cognitive processes relevant for goal-directed control of thought and actions, as a promising candidate for such a mechanism. We review evidence that EF development is shaped by both genetic and environmental factors and relies on protracted maturation of neural networks, particularly frontoparietal and cingulo-opercular systems. Disruptions in these systems are associated with elevated risk for internalising and externalising disorders. We therefore propose EFs as a cognitive endophenotype of developmental psychopathology—heritable, measurable, and lying on the pathway from gene to disorder. We review evidence showing that impaired EF is a shared feature across psychiatric conditions and predictive of future symptomatology, supporting its transdiagnostic relevance. We also propose a mechanistic refinement of the EF construct, moving beyond capacity-based interpretations to a model in which EF performance reflects dynamic and contextually informed cost-benefit computations. Disruptions in reward and effort processing—manifesting as anhedonia and apathy—are common across mental health conditions and may compromise EF performance by altering these computations. This integrative perspective helps explain the limited efficacy of traditional EF training interventions on improving mental health symptoms and underscores the importance of motivational and contextual factors. We conclude by outlining a future research agenda focussed on disentangling the specific subprocesses underpinning EFs and their mechanistic links to developmental psychopathology. Recognising EFs as a transdiagnostic cognitive endophenotype governed by rational control processes opens new avenues for precise, developmentally informed, and targeted interventions in youth mental health.
abstract_zh: 摘要：大多数精神健康问题在成年前出现，尤其在儿童和青少年期间患病率上升。加之不同疾病之间高度共病，迫切需要识别支撑发展性精神病理学风险与韧性的跨诊断机制。本文提出执行功能（EFs）——一组与目标导向思维与行为控制相关的认知过程——作为此类机制的有前景候选。我们综述了EF发展受遗传与环境因素共同塑造，并依赖于前额-顶叶和扣带-口腔系统等神经网络的长期成熟。对这些系统的破坏与内化和外化障碍的风险升高相关。因此，我们将EFs视为发展性精神病理学的认知内在表型——可遗传、可测量，并位于基因到疾病的路径上。我们还回顾了证据表明EF受损是多种精神疾病的共同特征，并能预测未来症状，支持其跨诊断相关性。我们提出对EF构念的机制性细化，超越基于容量的解释，提出EF表现反映动态且受情境影响的成本-收益计算。奖励与努力处理的失调——表现为快感缺失和冷漠——在多种精神健康状况中普遍存在，可能通过改变这些计算来削弱EF表现。此整合视角有助于解释传统EF训练干预在改善精神健康症状方面的有限效果，并强调动机与情境因素的重要性。我们以未来研究议程作结，聚焦于阐明EF所依赖的具体子过程及其与发展性精神病理学的机制性联系。将EF视为受理性控制过程支配的跨诊断认知内在表型，为青少年精神健康提供精准、发展导向且针对性的干预新途径。
